meta.abstract: ASP Isotopes Inc. (NASDAQ: ASPI) is a US-listed specialty isotope enrichment company that uses its proprietary Aerodynamic Separation Process (ASP) — a stable-isotope enrichment platform — to produce isotopically-enriched materials for three principal end-markets: (1) advanced semiconductor materials (silicon-28 for next-generation transistor channels and quantum computing substrates), (2) medical isotopes (molybdenum-100, ytterbium-176, nickel-64 for diagnostic imaging and targeted radiotherapy), and (3) HALEU (High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium) for advanced reactor fuel via subsidiary Quantum Leap Energy. Co-founded and led by Paul Mann. Strategic narrative through 2024-2026 centered on scaling enrichment capacity, customer contracts in semiconductor and medical isotope markets, and the HALEU thesis tied to US advanced-reactor buildout.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
ASP Isotopes entered the decade-long enrichment ramp carrying three distinct growth propositions stacked inside a single proprietary technology. By the frozen-window date of 23 May 2026, Chairman and Chief Executive Paul Mann had repositioned what began as a specialty isotope producer into what he called, on the company's fourth-quarter 2025 earnings call, something far larger: "We are no longer a development stage company. We are a critical materials platform."

The claim was ambitious relative to the underlying revenue base. But the structural architecture behind it — the Aerodynamic Separation Process (ASP) deployed across silicon-28 for advanced semiconductors, medical radioisotopes, and High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium via the Quantum Leap Energy (QLE) subsidiary — made ASP Isotopes one of the few listed companies with credible, if still largely forward-looking, exposure to all three of the decade's most capital-intensive isotope supply themes. NASDAQ ticker: ASPI. Headquarters: Washington, D.C. area, with enrichment operations anchored in Pretoria, South Africa.

## Heritage: A South African Process Goes Public

The company's core intellectual property traces its lineage to decades of aerodynamic separation research at South African universities and was commercialised by Mann and his co-founders under the ASP Isotopes banner. The Aerodynamic Separation Process — distinct from gaseous diffusion and laser enrichment in that it exploits the centrifugal mass separation of isotope streams through high-speed gas flow — proved adaptable across a broad isotopic mass range, from isotopically light carbon-13 to heavy uranium hexafluoride. The Pretoria enrichment plant, built out through 2023–2025, served as the demonstration and early-commercial hub across all three platforms. Additional enrichment capacity in Iceland remained in planning through the frozen window, pending permitting.

## Three Platforms, One Facility

**Silicon-28** targeted the advanced semiconductor node market, where isotopic purification of silicon channels reduces phonon scattering and theoretically extends transistor performance below the 3-nanometre threshold. By August 2025 ASPI had shipped its first enriched Si-28 samples to a customer, with independent analysis confirming enrichment levels aligned with theoretical calculations. Three purchase agreements were in place — one with a major U.S. semiconductor company, one with a large global industrial-gases company, and one with a further U.S. buyer — against a target of first commercial shipments in the second quarter of 2026.

**Medical isotopes** comprised molybdenum-100 (Mo-100, for Tc-99m SPECT imaging), ytterbium-176 (Yb-176, for lutetium-177 targeted radiotherapy), nickel-64 (Ni-64, for copper-64 PET imaging), and carbon-13 (C-13, for diagnostics). First commercial C-14 shipments were targeted for mid-2026; Yb-176 for mid-to-late Q3 2026. ASPI also built a downstream radiopharmacy distribution footprint through its 51 per cent stake in PET Labs and the October 2025 acquisition of East Coast Nuclear Pharmacy in Florida for $2.5 million, targeting radiopharmacy revenues of $10 million or more for 2026.

**Quantum Leap Energy**, structured as a subsidiary with its own Austin, Texas headquarters, carried the HALEU thesis. In May 2025 ASPI signed definitive agreements with TerraPower: a conditional $22 million loan to finance construction of a HALEU enrichment facility at Pelindaba, South Africa; an initial-core supply contract valued at approximately $375 million to fuel TerraPower's Natrium reactor in Wyoming in the 2027–28 timeframe; and a ten-year long-term supply contract for up to 150 metric tonnes of HALEU from 2028 through 2037, notionally valued at up to $3.75 billion. Mann framed the demand case starkly: "Nuclear fuel has one of the most severely compromised supply chains of any material in the world." QLE confidentially submitted a draft S-1 registration statement to the SEC in November 2025, flagging a planned public listing subject to market conditions.

## Financial Snapshot

Against this activity, fiscal 2025 revenues reached $23.8 million — a 480 per cent year-on-year increase from $4.1 million in 2024 — though the headline masked the composition: $5.7 million derived from product sales (radiopharmaceuticals and isotope samples), with the remainder drawn from Skyline Construction Services, an infrastructure-execution subsidiary. Operating losses widened to $59.9 million; the net loss reached $175.1 million, reflecting non-cash and financing charges. The company ended December 2025 holding $333 million in cash and marketable securities, after raising more than $345 million of equity capital during the year. A 2031 EBITDA target exceeding $300 million — spanning electronic gases, LNG, medical isotopes, and radiopharmaceuticals, and explicitly excluding QLE — framed the long-term ambition.

> "2026 is a transformational year for the company," Mann told analysts. "We look forward to … becoming a major supplier of isotopic and critical materials to the world."

## What This Dossier Asks

The chapters that follow interrogate the gap between ambition and execution. How mature is the Aerodynamic Separation Process across its three isotope families, and what are the realistic throughput ceilings at Pretoria? Which of the signed purchase agreements have converted to revenue-generating deliveries, and on what timeline? Can QLE deliver HALEU at Pelindaba in 2027 against a permitting and construction schedule that remains subject to South African regulatory approvals? What does a QLE spin-off achieve in valuation and capital terms that the parent structure does not? And how does ASPI's cost position and technology differentiation compare against Centrus Energy — the only other U.S. HALEU enricher — as well as the European enrichment incumbents URENCO and Orano?

---

chapters.title: From ASP commercialisation through the Pretoria facility scaling to the three-platform thesis
chapters.body:
## Roots in Pelindaba: the Aerodynamic Separation Process

The technology that anchors ASP Isotopes traces its lineage not to a Silicon Valley lab but to the pariah-state physics of apartheid South Africa. During the 1980s, the South African Atomic Energy Corporation operated the Helikon vortex-tube cascade at Pelindaba, outside Pretoria, to enrich uranium for the Koeberg nuclear plant while the country was frozen out of international supply chains. The Helikon process worked, but at ruinous energy cost — roughly 10,000 kilowatt-hours per separative work unit, an order of magnitude more profligate than the gas centrifuges then becoming standard in Europe.

Dr. Hendrik Strydom, a physicist at the AEC who had specialised in laser separation of heavy isotopes, left the corporation in 1993 and co-founded Klydon (Pty) Ltd, a private isotope enrichment company in Pretoria. Over the following two decades, the Klydon scientists refined a stationary-wall aerodynamic process — gas injected tangentially so that heavier and lighter isotopologs separate under centrifugal force without the mechanical bearing complexity of a spinning rotor. The result was an enrichment factor that the team drove from roughly 1.03 toward a target of 1.10 to 1.15, with projected energy consumption below 1,000 kWh per SWU and a modelled production cost under $100 per SWU. [World Nuclear News](https://world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/New-South-African-enrichment-process) The approach proved especially potent for isotopes whose mass difference made them tractable to aerodynamic rather than electromagnetic or chemical separation — a class that usefully included silicon, molybdenum, ytterbium and uranium. Klydon commissioned a pilot oxygen-18 plant in Pretoria in October 2015 and followed with a silicon-28 plant in July 2018, demonstrating multi-kilogram annual throughput on both.

## Delaware Incorporation and the Pretoria Acquisition

Paul Mann arrived at Klydon's door with a Wall Street investor's eye rather than a physicist's. Mann had spent more than twenty years in capital markets, with stints at Soros Fund Management, Highbridge Capital Management and Morgan Stanley, focusing on healthcare and specialty chemicals. He and co-founder Robert Ainscow incorporated ASP Isotopes Inc. in Delaware on 13 September 2021, obtained South African nuclear regulatory approvals the same month, and quickly moved to purchase Klydon's two incomplete enrichment plants in Pretoria — the first acquisition completing in October 2021, the second in July 2022. [ASP Isotopes S-1, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1921865/000121390022055355/fs12022_aspisotopesinc.htm)

The intellectual property anchor was formalised simultaneously: in July 2022 ASP Isotopes UK Ltd executed a licence agreement with Klydon granting an exclusive, royalty-free, 999-year worldwide right to use, develop, modify, sub-licence and commercialise the entire ASP technology portfolio across every isotope. The combination of plant ownership and perpetual IP licence gave the nascent company an unusually durable competitive moat — not merely a technology partnership that could be renegotiated, but a structural asset embedded in the balance sheet.

Construction progressed quickly. The company completed its first enrichment plant — a lighter-isotope configuration — in March 2023, approximately three months ahead of schedule, a cadence that Mann would repeatedly cite as evidence of the team's execution discipline. Even before commissioning was complete, the commercial pipeline had opened: in November 2022 ASP Isotopes announced a 25-year supply agreement with BRICEM — the Beijing Research Institute of Chemical Engineering and Metallurgy — for highly enriched molybdenum-100 valued at up to $27 million per annum, with deliveries scheduled to commence in July 2023. [ASP Isotopes IR](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/12/asp-isotopes-inc-enters-into-25-year-supply-agreement) Mo-100 is the principal precursor for technetium-99m, the workhorse radioisotope of SPECT cardiac and oncology imaging; the agreement signalled that the company's first commercial plant had found a credible off-taker before it had shipped a single gram.

## Going Public on a Shoestring

ASP Isotopes began trading on the NASDAQ Capital Market on 10 November 2022 under the ticker ASPI. The offering priced at $4.00 per share; 1,250,000 shares were sold with a 187,500-share over-allotment option, generating gross proceeds of approximately $5.0 million — a modest sum reflecting the company's development-stage status and the micro-cap underwriting syndicate led by Revere Securities. The company was then headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida, though operational gravity was firmly in Pretoria. [GlobeNewswire IPO release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2022/11/10/2553191/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Announces-Pricing-of-Initial-Public-Offering-and-Nasdaq-Listing.html)

The listed structure gave ASP Isotopes the currency — common stock — to pursue serial equity raises as production milestones justified higher valuations. Between the 2022 IPO and late 2025 the company executed multiple follow-on transactions. The largest came in October 2025, when ASPI sold 17,167,380 shares at $12.25 each, raising approximately $210.3 million in gross proceeds. [Simply Wall St / Webull reporting, Oct 2025](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nasdaq-aspi/asp-isotopes/news/what-asp-isotopes-aspis-210-million-equity-raise-and-expansi) The offering was timed to coincide with the announcement of the company's largest silicon-28 supply contract and the acquisition of a Florida radiopharmacy — the first external location for PET Labs, ASPI's South African radiopharmacy affiliate — signalling a pivot from pure isotope producer toward vertically integrated radiopharmaceutical supplier.

## Three Platforms in Motion: Isotope Offtake and the Quantum Leap Subsidiary

The company's 2024–2025 operating narrative was organised around parallel ramps across three distinct isotope streams, each at a different point on the production readiness curve.

In the semiconductor segment, ASP Isotopes completed construction of its second ASP facility — dedicated to silicon-28 — in November 2024 and commenced commissioning; commercial production followed in March 2025. [GlobeNewswire, Nov 2024](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/11/26/2987443/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Completes-Construction-and-Starts-the-Commissioning-of-Silicon-28-Enrichment-Facility.html) Silicon-28 at enrichment levels above 99.9% eliminates the nuclear-spin noise from the naturally occurring silicon-29 and silicon-30 isotopologs, providing a near-perfect substrate for solid-state spin qubits and advanced transistor channels. In August 2025 the company shipped its first samples to a US customer, with independent laboratory analysis confirming enrichment in line with theoretical projections. By September 2025 it had signed three US contracts for Si-28; that autumn it announced what it described as its largest Si-28 agreement to date with an undisclosed American customer, targeting Q1 2026 delivery. In his September 2025 shareholder letter, Mann wrote that Yb-176 and Si-28 together represented "**$50 to $70 million of potential revenues during 2026 and 2027**." Engineering modifications to non-core components — valves, compressors and piping — were underway across the facility as of the frozen snapshot date, with commercial shipments expected in the third quarter of 2026. [ASP Isotopes IR](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/107/asp-isotopes-implements-engineering-enhancements-to)

In the medical segment, the company built a first "Quantum Enrichment" laser-based facility for ytterbium-176, completing it approximately nine months ahead of schedule by April 2025 and shipping initial commercial samples that same summer. Yb-176 is the precursor for lutetium-177, the targeted-beta radiotherapy isotope underpinning a fast-growing class of radioligand therapies. The success of the Yb-176 plant accelerated plans for nickel-64 and lithium-6/7 plants, and in mid-2025 the company entered a four-year supply agreement with Isotopia Molecular Imaging for gadolinium-160, a terbium-161 precursor, at a minimum contracted value of approximately $1 million per annum beginning in 2026.

The third platform took institutional form in September 2023 when ASP Isotopes established Quantum Leap Energy LLC as a wholly owned subsidiary to pursue high-assay low-enriched uranium enriched to near 19.75% U-235 — the fuel grade mandated by most advanced reactor designs including TerraPower's Natrium, X-energy's Xe-100 and Oklo's Aurora. QLE held entities in the United Kingdom, South Africa, the United States and Iceland, the last chosen for its combination of low-cost geothermal power and a permissive regulatory environment for isotope-processing investment. No Western commercial producer of HALEU existed at scale; Mann argued the supply gap was structural.

> "Our singular focus in 2026 is execution, and we intend to deliver," Mann said in early 2026, framing the year as the company's inflection from construction-and-announcement mode to revenue recognition. [ASP Isotopes IR](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/91/asp-isotopes-inc-announces-paul-mann-to-return-from)

The anchor commercial agreement for QLE arrived on 19 May 2025: definitive agreements with TerraPower included a conditional $22 million loan — maturing in 2032 — for construction of a HALEU production facility, coupled with a 10-year supply framework for up to 150 metric tons of HALEU from 2028 through 2037. [ASP Isotopes IR](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/61/asp-isotopes-inc-enters-into-definitive-agreements-with) QLE's initial production site was designated as Pelindaba — the same complex where South Africa once ran its clandestine weapons-grade enrichment programme — subject to regulatory approval; a Texas facility was identified as a second location. In February 2026, QLE's South African subsidiary and the South African Nuclear Energy Corporation (Necsa) executed a Pre-Implementation Services Contract, formalising collaboration on HALEU research, development and commercial-scale production. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/23/3242521/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Announces-Quantum-Leap-Energy-and-Necsa-Advance-Strategic-Collaboration-Aimed-at-Production-of-HALEU-Nuclear-Fuel.html)

## The Three-Platform Thesis at the Frozen Snapshot

As of 23 May 2026, ASP Isotopes occupied a specific and deliberately unusual position in the capital markets: the only US-listed pure-play specialist enrichment company with operating enrichment plants, signed commercial contracts across all three of its declared platforms — semiconductors, medical isotopes and HALEU — and a subsidiary pipeline (Quantum Leap Energy, whose NASDAQ S-1 was filed for a planned independent listing) that separated the long-dated uranium-fuel option from the near-term specialty-isotope revenue story. Revenue remained modest and operating losses persisted, reflecting enrichment lead times and customer qualification cycles that stretched 12 to 24 months beyond the signing of offtake agreements. Yet the company's stated roadmap — first silicon-28 commercial shipments in Q3 2026, Yb-176 scaling toward roughly one kilogram per year, carbon-14 revenue already flowing, and HALEU first-feed at Pelindaba contingent on Necsa approvals — represented, at a minimum, the most fully realised attempt by a Western enrichment start-up to address three distinct critical-materials supply gaps simultaneously.

> "ASP Isotopes is positioned to be a beneficiary of tomorrow's megatrends in next-generation nuclear energy, nuclear medicine and next-generation industrial processes," Mann told shareholders in May 2025. [GlobeNewswire shareholder letter, May 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/29/3090298/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Issues-Letter-to-Shareholders.html)

Whether execution would convert that positioning into durable cash generation remained, as of the frozen date, the central unanswered question for investors.

chapters.title: Aerodynamic Separation Process, Si-28, medical isotopes, and the HALEU subsidiary
chapters.body:
The technology at the centre of ASP Isotopes traces its genealogy not to Silicon Valley but to apartheid-era Pretoria, where South African state scientists developed a vortex-based uranium enrichment method called the Helikon process during the 1970s and 1980s. That programme was later commercialised by [Klydon Proprietary Ltd.](https://aspisotopes.com/technology), which spent eighteen years refining the underlying intellectual property before licensing it exclusively to ASPI for all non-nuclear-fuel isotope applications globally — and, through the subsidiary Quantum Leap Energy, for nuclear fuel applications as well. When Paul Mann took the company public on NASDAQ in November 2022, the core proposition was that a decades-old South African separation science, largely overlooked by the Western enrichment establishment, could be redeployed across three structurally undersupplied markets: advanced semiconductors, medical radioisotopes, and high-assay low-enriched uranium for next-generation reactors.

## The Aerodynamic Separation Process and its laser complement

ASPI built its commercial platform around two distinct enrichment technologies, deployed selectively by isotope mass. The aerodynamic separation process — the ASP — functions as a stationary-wall centrifuge. Isotope feedstock converted into volatile gas enters a stationary tube at high speed through tangential injection openings; within the tube, the flow organises into two counter-rotating vortex streams spinning at several hundred metres per second. Centrifugal forces cause heavier isotopes to migrate toward the outer wall while lighter isotopes concentrate at the central axis, and the two fractions are extracted separately. This constitutes a single enrichment stage; commercial production requires many such stages arranged in cascade. For light isotopes — silicon and carbon — ASPI deployed the ASP vortex process. For heavier isotopes including ytterbium-176, nickel-64, and uranium, the company used a separate laser-based method it branded Quantum Enrichment (QE): finely tuned lasers selectively ionise the target isotope from a vapour, and the charged atoms are collected on a plate. During the commissioning of its third Pretoria facility in late 2024, ASPI reported an achieved QE enrichment factor of 52 per stage, in line with its internal design target of greater than 50.

The competitive backdrop against which ASPI measured its claims was anchored by gas centrifuge incumbents of formidable scale. [URENCO](https://www.urenco.com) operated approximately 17 million separative work units of annual capacity across four national sites; [Orano's](https://www.orano.group) Georges Besse II plant in Tricastin contributed roughly 7.5 million SWU per year. Capital costs for centrifuge enrichment ran to approximately $1 billion per million SWU of installed capacity — a barrier that had historically confined new entrants. SILEX Systems and its joint venture partner Cameco, advancing molecular laser isotope separation through Global Laser Enrichment, reached technology-readiness level six at their Wilmington, North Carolina pilot in 2024 and acquired the 700-acre Paducah Laser Enrichment Facility site in Kentucky for their commercial facility, with earliest possible commercial operations estimated at 2028 and the company opting not to pursue HALEU under DOE competitive solicitations. Against those benchmarks, ASPI asserted that a single QE plant could be constructed for approximately $10 million, a figure the company had not subjected to independent third-party validation in any publicly available filing as of the frozen snapshot date.

## Silicon-28: from research concept to Pretoria production

The semiconductor application for silicon-28 rested on two distinct demand theses. The first was transistor performance at sub-3nm geometries: natural silicon is a mixture of three stable isotopes — roughly 92.2% Si-28, 4.7% Si-29, and 3.1% Si-30 — and the isotopic disorder introduces phonon scattering that limits thermal conductivity and carrier mobility. Isotopically enriched Si-28 at 99.995% purity eliminates those mixed-mass phonon pathways, improving thermal conductivity by roughly 150% over natural silicon according to company disclosures, with implications for heat management in densely packed advanced logic nodes. The second thesis was quantum computing substrates: Si-29 carries a nuclear spin of one-half, which introduces magnetic noise destructive to spin-qubit coherence. Academic research published from groups at the University of Manchester, Princeton, and the University of Melbourne had demonstrated that isotopically enriched 28-Si extended qubit coherence times dramatically — room-temperature coherence above 39 minutes had been reported in purified material — making high-purity Si-28 a precondition for scalable silicon spin-qubit architectures.

ASPI's second Pretoria facility, sited at Koedoespoort and described as approximately 40 times larger than its first plant on a SWU basis, completed construction on [November 26, 2024](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/11/26/2987443/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Completes-Construction-and-Starts-the-Commissioning-of-Silicon-28-Enrichment-Facility.html). Commercial production commenced [March 27, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/03/27/3050495/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Commences-Commercial-Production-of-Enriched-Silicon-28-at-its-Second-Aerodynamic-Separation-Process-ASP-Enrichment-Facility.html). The ASP process enriched silane (SiH4) rather than the silicon tetrafluoride or halosilane feedstocks used in competing approaches, a distinction ASPI highlighted because silane output is directly usable by semiconductor customers without additional chemical conversion. Production capacity guidance was revised upward twice during commissioning: from an original target of approximately 10 kilograms per year to greater than 50 kg/year, and then again by July 2025 to greater than 80 kg/year of 99.995% enriched material at maximum operating rate. The company disclosed engineering enhancements to the facility after initial production commenced, restarting the first 18 stages; commercial shipments were expected from the third quarter of 2026.

At commissioning, ASPI had executed two signed purchase agreements — one with an unnamed U.S. semiconductor company and one with a U.S. industrial gas company — and reported a total of three purchase orders by the time it filed its FY2025 annual report. No customer names appeared in any public disclosure. Pricing was initially set at approximately $500,000 per kilogram, and Mann indicated at the time of commissioning that the company was evaluating reductions to stimulate broader demand adoption.

> "To create faster, smaller next-generation semiconductors, the world is likely going to require materials that are currently not available in commercial quantities," Mann said. "ASP Isotopes is currently working on many isotopically pure elements that we believe will help semiconductor companies create the chips that the world will require in the future to enable technologies such as quantum computing and artificial intelligence."

## Medical isotopes: supply chain and the Russian gap

ASPI's medical isotope programme exploited a structural feature of the global radiopharmaceutical supply chain: Russia had historically supplied the dominant share of several enriched stable precursor isotopes, and Western users had no readily available alternative. Against that backdrop, the company announced agreements across multiple medical isotope streams.

The most publicised was a [25-year supply agreement](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/12/asp-isotopes-inc-enters-into-25-year-supply-agreement) with BRICEM — the Beijing Research Institute of Chemical Engineering and Metallurgy — for molybdenum-100, signed November 2022. The contract provided for up to $27 million annually, with planned capacity of greater than 20 kilograms per year of Mo-100 enriched to above 95%; deliveries were originally scheduled to commence in mid-2023. Mo-100 serves as a cyclotron target in the accelerator-based production of technetium-99m, the dominant diagnostic radioisotope in nuclear medicine with an estimated 30 to 40 million imaging procedures annually. However, no press release confirming commercial deliveries appeared in ASPI's public disclosure record, and a July 2025 company update on Pretoria production activity made no reference to Mo-100 output — a gap that left the agreement's operational status unresolved within the frozen snapshot period.

The ytterbium-176 programme was further advanced. Yb-176, when irradiated in a reactor, yields lutetium-177, the therapeutic radioisotope in Novartis's [Pluvicto](https://www.novartis.com/us-en/sites/novartis_us/files/pluvicto.pdf), approved for metastatic prostate cancer. ASPI's third Pretoria facility used the QE laser process to enrich Yb-176 to a target of 99.75%; commissioning in October 2024 achieved 92.4% intermediate enrichment before the facility transitioned to batch production at three to five hours per day. Capacity was approximately one kilogram per year against a market price of roughly $20,000 per gram — implying potential annual revenues approaching $20 million from a single facility if fully subscribed.

> "Currently, there exist significant supply-side challenges for many essential radioisotopes used in various oncology treatments," Mann said in October 2024. "We have received a considerable amount of interest from customers in North America, Europe and Asia for Ytterbium-176 and we look forward to easing supply chains and improving the quality of life for thousands of patients every year."

The carbon-14 programme reached commercial production on [February 26, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/02/26/3032873/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Commences-Commercial-Production-of-Enriched-Carbon-14-at-its-First-Aerodynamic-Separation-Process-ASP-Enrichment-Facility.html), underpinned by a multi-year take-or-pay agreement with Canadian company RC-14 Inc. carrying a minimum of approximately $2.4 million per year. C-14 is used as a radiotracer in pharmaceutical development for metabolic and ADME studies; Russia had historically supplied the entire global enriched C-14 market. First commercial shipments were delayed to the second quarter of 2026 due to feedstock logistics complications — what Mann described as "a timing issue, not a science issue." The company cited gross margins of 85 to 90% for the C-14 product, a benchmark it applied broadly to comparable light-isotope streams.

The nickel-64 programme — whose enrichment yields copper-64 for PET imaging — remained at an earlier stage; import permits for laser enrichment equipment had been received by late 2025 but no supply agreements or customer names had been publicly disclosed.

## Quantum Leap Energy and the HALEU thesis

ASPI incorporated Quantum Leap Energy LLC in September 2023, granting it exclusive global rights to both the ASP and QE technologies for nuclear fuel applications. The subsidiary was positioned to address a specific gap in the United States and allied-nation nuclear fuel supply chains: high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU), enriched between 5% and 19.75% U-235, required by a generation of advanced reactor designs including TerraPower's Natrium sodium fast reactor, X-energy's Xe-100 pebble-bed, and several microreactor concepts. The U.S. Department of Energy projected domestic HALEU demand reaching 50 metric tons per year by 2035 and 500 metric tons per year by 2050, against a supply base that as of 2025 consisted principally of Russian exports and a single American demonstration cascade — Centrus Energy's AC-100M centrifuge string at Piketon, Ohio, which had produced and delivered 900 kilograms of HALEU under a DOE contract and was awarded a $900 million task order for capacity expansion.

QLE's route to market moved through a sequence of disclosed milestones. TerraPower provided a $2 million research contract in 2024, followed by a non-binding term sheet in October 2024 committing TerraPower to fund construction of a HALEU production facility and purchase all output over a ten-year post-completion horizon. On [May 19, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/19/3084426/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-enters-into-Definitive-Agreements-with-TerraPower-including-Loan-Agreement-for-Construction-of-a-HALEU-Production-Facility-and-Supply-Agreements-for-HALEU.html), the parties signed definitive agreements: a $22.0 million conditional term loan from TerraPower at 10% interest maturing in May 2032, structured as a multi-advance facility tied to construction milestones and regulatory permits, alongside a ten-year HALEU supply framework covering deliveries from 2028 through 2037, up to 150 metric tons total at approximately 15 metric tons annually, with a headline value of roughly $3.75 billion at prevailing market prices. The planned production facility was sited at Pelindaba — the Necsa (South African Nuclear Energy Corporation) campus in North West Province — where QLE had secured access to established nuclear infrastructure, utilities, and safeguards oversight under South Africa's IAEA comprehensive safeguards agreement. A production start date of 2027 was targeted, subject to licensing from the South African National Nuclear Regulator.

> "Nuclear fuel has one of the most severely compromised supply chains of any material in the world," Mann said at the announcement. "The world is in urgent need of additional suppliers."

A secondary site was flagged in August 2025, when QLE signed a non-binding MOU with Fermi America for a joint venture at the HyperGrid Campus in Carson County, Texas, adjacent to the Department of Energy's Pantex Plant — a location with existing nuclear infrastructure and workforce. QLE also signed a framework with an undisclosed European advanced reactor developer in early 2026 covering potential HALEU deliveries from 2028.

QLE confidentially submitted a draft Form S-1 to the SEC in November 2025. ASPI's board intended to distribute QLE shares to existing shareholders in a spin-out transaction expected in the first half of 2026, with ASPI retaining a 10% perpetual royalty on all QLE revenues. By the time of the frozen snapshot, QLE's Austin, Texas global headquarters had been established, and Ryno Pretorius had been appointed as the subsidiary's chief executive, separating day-to-day leadership of the nuclear fuel business from ASPI's broader isotope enrichment operations.

| Enrichment technology | Incumbent scale | Estimated capex per unit | ASPI claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gas centrifuge (URENCO, Orano) | ~17M / ~7.5M SWU/yr | ~$1B per 1M SWU/yr | — |
| SILEX / GLE laser (Paducah) | Pilot; commercial est. 2028 | Not disclosed | QE separation factor ~52/stage vs. GLE ~20 |
| Centrus AC-100M (Piketon) | 900 kg HALEU/yr demo | $900M DOE award to expand | — |
| QE laser (ASPI / QLE) | 1 kg/yr Yb-176; 15 MT/yr HALEU (planned) | ~$10M per QE plant (co. claim, unaudited) | Capital-efficient vs. centrifuge at scale |

The convergence of the Si-28 semiconductor programme, the medical isotope suite, and the HALEU subsidiary under a single enrichment technology platform was ASPI's central strategic argument: that proprietary separation science developed in South Africa's defence programme could be repackaged, scaled modularly, and redirected at supply dislocations across three sectors simultaneously. Whether the QE enrichment factor advantage over SILEX was sufficient to displace centrifuge economics at industrial HALEU scale remained, as of May 2026, the central unresolved question in the investment case.

---
*Sources: [SEC EDGAR — ASPI filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=ASPI&type=10-K); [ASP Isotopes IR](https://ir.aspisotopes.com/news-events/press-releases); [TerraPower definitive agreements (May 2025)](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/19/3084426/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-enters-into-Definitive-Agreements-with-TerraPower-including-Loan-Agreement-for-Construction-of-a-HALEU-Production-Facility-and-Supply-Agreements-for-HALEU.html); [Si-28 facility commissioning (Nov 2024)](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/11/26/2987443/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Completes-Construction-and-Starts-the-Commissioning-of-Silicon-28-Enrichment-Facility.html); [Yb-176 QE commissioning (Oct 2024)](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/10/17/2964820/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Enriches-Ytterbium-176-During-Commissioning-Phase-of-First-Quantum-Enrichment-Facility-and-Expects-to-Offer-Highly-Enriched-Ytterbium-176-for-Commercial-Sale-in-20.html); [C-14 commercial production (Feb 2025)](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/02/26/3032873/0/en/ASP-Isotopes-Inc-Commences-Commercial-Production-of-Enriched-Carbon-14-at-its-First-Aerodynamic-Separation-Process-ASP-Enrichment-Facility.html); [World Nuclear Association](https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/nuclear-fuel-cycle/conversion-enrichment-and-fabrication/uranium-enrichment).*

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, operating losses, capex, capital structure, dilution dynamics
chapters.body:
## A Revenue Line Built From Scratch

When ASP Isotopes completed its modest initial public offering on the NASDAQ in November 2022 — raising just $5.0 million at $4.00 per share through sole bookrunner Revere Securities — the company carried precisely zero revenue on its income statement. That was not an embarrassment but a design feature: the enrichment facilities at Pretoria, South Africa were still coming online, and customers in specialty isotopes do not place orders against capacity that does not yet exist. The story of ASP Isotopes' finances through 2024 is therefore not a conventional revenue ramp but something more layered — a construction ledger, a dilution chronicle, and a bet on the lag between announced offtake and recognised receipts.

The first dollars arrived in FY2023: $433,031 in specialist isotope and related services revenue, recognised after the Pretoria plant began initial enrichment runs. The number was negligible against the company's cost base, but it marked a categorical shift from development stage to early commercial. The October 2023 acquisition of a 51% stake in PET Labs Pharmaceuticals — a South African radiopharmaceutical distributor — added a stub two months of consolidation to the year's results, though the primary contribution was strategic: a downstream channel into nuclear medicine customers rather than a near-term revenue driver.

By FY2024 the trajectory had steepened. Core specialist-isotope and collaboration revenue from ASP Isotopes' own enrichment operations reached approximately $3.94 million, up from $433,000 the prior year — a near-tenfold increase, though from a base so low that the percentage move overstates the commercial maturity. Fully consolidated with PET Labs Pharmaceuticals across all four quarters, total group revenue likely approached $8 million, though segment and consolidation methodologies produced different readings across data aggregators. [SEC EDGAR — ASPI FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001921865/000095017025047694/aspi-20241231.htm) The first quarter of 2025 produced $1.10 million in revenue, against $840,000 in Q1 2024, suggesting an annualised run-rate somewhere between $4 million and $5 million from the core enrichment business heading into mid-year.

| Period | Revenue (Core Enrichment) | Net Loss | Shares Outstanding (Period-End) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | $0 | $(4.9)M | ~35.9M |
| FY2023 | $0.43M | $(16.3)M | 48.9M |
| FY2024 | $3.94M | $(35.1)M | 72.1M |
| Q1 2025 | $1.10M | $(8.5)M | ~69.5M (wtd avg) |

The gap between offtake announcement and revenue recognition remains the central discipline for reading ASPI's income statement. The company has disclosed multiple memoranda of understanding for Si-28, Mo-100, Yb-176, and Ni-64 supply, but enrichment contracts in specialty isotopes typically require twelve to twenty-four months of customer qualification before material volumes are invoiced. Revenue therefore lags the news cycle by a year or more.

## The Widening Loss Curve

Operating losses have deepened in near-lockstep with the build-out programme. In FY2022, the operating loss was $5.1 million — essentially a skeletal management team, the early Pretoria construction spend, and intellectual property development costs. By FY2023 it had expanded to $16.0 million as the company added technical headcount, accelerated facility construction across multiple isotope lines, and absorbed the administrative costs of a newly public small-cap. FY2024 brought the operating loss to $26.4 million.

The reported net loss in FY2024 was considerably larger: $35.1 million, against an operating loss of $26.4 million. The difference — roughly $8.7 million — reflects fair-value accounting treatment applied to Quantum Leap Energy convertible notes held on the consolidated balance sheet. Because ASPI elected to carry the QLE notes at fair value rather than amortised cost, mark-to-market movements flowed through the income statement, inflating the reported net loss figure in a manner disconnected from underlying cash burn. As of June 30, 2024, the QLE convertible note position was carried at approximately $29.1 million against an initial principal of $20.55 million — a reminder that structured subsidiary financing can produce income-statement noise that obscures the operational picture. [SEC EDGAR — ASPI Q2 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=ASPI&type=10-Q)

The company does not disclose a formal adjusted EBITDA metric. Given the minimal depreciation and amortisation at this stage of the asset build, EBITDA approximates the operating loss in any case. Cash operating burn ran at roughly $15 million annually as of early 2025 by management's own framing.

## Capex: Three Plants and an Iceland Option

Capital expenditure tells the construction story most directly. In FY2022, with the first Pretoria facility under build, capex reached $4.47 million. It dipped to $2.33 million in FY2023 as one enrichment line approached mechanical completion and the company paused before committing to subsequent expansions. The acceleration came in FY2024, when capex climbed to approximately $11.4 million as ASP pushed simultaneously on three separate Pretoria enrichment facilities — silicon-28, carbon-14, and an ytterbium-176/erbium line — while beginning pre-development work on the Iceland site designated for Quantum Leap Energy's HALEU programme.

The Iceland facility is architecturally distinct from Pretoria. The aerodynamic separation process for uranium enrichment requires a regulatory environment that South Africa, while accommodating for stable isotopes, is not configured to support for nuclear material at commercial scale. Iceland offers renewable power (critical for an energy-intensive centrifuge-analogue process), geopolitical alignment with US and European advanced-reactor programmes, and a regulatory path through the International Atomic Energy Agency frameworks. Capital commitments for the Iceland HALEU site were not fully quantified in FY2024 filings, but the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation credit facility — evidenced by a $1.6 million restricted cash reserve held as six months of forward payments — indicates external project-finance support was secured for that programme.

The Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa similarly provided a debt facility for the Pretoria operations, reflected in a $1.2 million restricted cash reserve as of early 2025. Both facilities reduce the equity-dilution burden on the US-listed parent, though the terms and amounts were not fully disclosed in public filings.

## Serial Equity and the Dilution Ledger

The capital structure of ASP Isotopes through 2024 is a sequential record of equity issuances, each reflecting both the company's improving narrative and its persistent inability to self-fund from operations.

The November 2022 IPO raised $5.0 million at $4.00 per share — a minimal float by any standard, with 1.25 million shares offered plus an overallotment option. By March 2023, the share price had fallen materially, and the company returned to the market via a PIPE at $1.58 per share, with accompanying warrants exercisable at $1.75 — raising another $5.0 million but crystallising the dilution overhang that would define the next eighteen months. A second PIPE in October 2023, at $0.91 per share, raised $9.1 million with Tees River Critical Resources Fund as anchor investor; the placement price, at roughly a 77% discount to the IPO level, underscored the degree to which speculative small-cap dynamics had compressed the stock.

The narrative inflection came in July 2024, when Canaccord Genuity led a fully underwritten public offering of 13.8 million shares (including a fully exercised overallotment) at $2.50 per share, generating $34.5 million in gross proceeds. A second Canaccord-led offering in November 2024 priced 2.75 million shares at $6.75, raising $18.6 million — the highest per-share level since the IPO and a signal that institutional appetite had returned as the Pretoria plants came online and offtake announcements accumulated. Combined equity raised at the ASPI parent level in 2024 reached approximately $53.1 million.

| Transaction | Date | Price | Shares | Gross Proceeds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IPO | Nov 2022 | $4.00 | 1.25M (+OA) | $5.0M |
| PIPE | Mar 2023 | $1.58 | 3.16M + warrants | $5.0M |
| PIPE | Oct 2023 | $0.91 | 9.95M | $9.1M |
| Public offering | Jul 2024 | $2.50 | 13.80M | $34.5M |
| Public offering | Nov 2024 | $6.75 | 2.75M | $18.6M |

The share count rose from approximately 35.9 million at the end of FY2022 to 48.9 million at end-FY2023, then to 72.1 million at end-FY2024 — a doubling in two years driven almost entirely by the equity financing programme rather than management option exercise or warrant conversion. By May 2026, the outstanding share count had grown further, toward 88.6 million, reflecting both the large October 2025 offering ($210.3 million gross at approximately $12.25 per share, 17.2 million new shares) and ongoing programme activity.

## Quantum Leap Energy: Subsidiary Finance as Complexity

The Quantum Leap Energy convertible note offering, closed in March 2024, introduced a layer of structural complexity that warrants separate treatment. The $20.55 million raised — from non-U.S. investors under Regulation S exemption, at 6% interest in year one and 8% thereafter, maturing March 2029 — was designed to fund HALEU site development without immediately diluting ASPI's listed equity. Auto-conversion provisions tied to a future QLE public listing or IPO meant the notes sit in a category that is neither straightforward debt nor equity. A June 2024 additional closing added approximately $5.4 million to the QLE facility. In November 2025, $64.3 million in new QLE convertible notes, led by American Ventures LLC, refinanced the 2024 notes — a transaction that closed after the frozen window of this analysis but whose structure was telegraphed through the 2024 fiscal year disclosures.

## Cash Runway and the Burn Equation

The liquidity position at the end of FY2024 was the strongest in the company's history: $61.89 million in cash and equivalents, against $7.91 million at end-FY2023 and just $2.39 million at end-FY2022. The July and November 2024 equity raises were primarily responsible for the step-change.

Mann characterised the position in the Q1 2025 earnings call:

> "We finished the year with about four years of operating free cash operating burn sitting on the balance sheet."

At an approximately $15 million annual operating cash burn rate, the $61.9 million year-end balance implied a runway to late 2028 before additional equity would be required for operations — provided capex commitments did not materially accelerate. By March 31, 2025, cash had declined modestly to $55.97 million, consistent with ongoing facility construction spend and operating costs, but still comfortably above any near-term liquidity constraint.

The company's December 2024 letter to shareholders — issued after a year in which it raised roughly $84 million across debt and equity instruments — struck a markedly different tone from the survival-mode private placements of 2023:

> "The Company's balance sheet has never been stronger."

That claim was defensible on the numbers. The more demanding test — whether the revenue line would begin to converge on the operating cost base before the next equity requirement arrived — remained the central question as the Pretoria facilities moved from construction to commercial-scale production through 2025.

chapters.title: Valuation — multiples, peer comparison, and bull/base/bear scenarios
chapters.body:
## A Measure Without a Yardstick

Valuing ASP Isotopes on conventional screening multiples produces an exercise in frustration. Through the fiscal-year 2025 reporting cycle, the company had not yet generated the sustained positive EBITDA or recurring net income that would make price-to-earnings or EV/EBITDA ratios meaningful. The standard toolkit of equity analysis therefore yields numbers that either divide by near-zero or collapse into negative territory. What remains are revenue multiples, book-value comparisons, and — most honestly — a market-implied DCF back-solved from whatever price the stock prints on a given day. Each of these methods carries its own distortion. None should be used in isolation.

With that caveat established, a working estimate of ASPI's market capitalisation at the frozen snapshot requires reasoning from the most recently reported share count rather than a single confirmed closing price, because the stock's intraday range through 2024-2025 was wide enough to swing implied market cap by a hundred million dollars on catalyst news. Based on publicly filed SEC documents — 10-K and 10-Q filings through fiscal year 2025 — shares outstanding following serial equity raises through that period stood in the range of 90 to 100 million. At a trailing price range of roughly $3 to $6 per share observed across the first five months of 2026, the implied market capitalisation sits between approximately $270 million and $600 million. Enterprise value, net of cash balances that the company actively deploys for Pretoria capacity expansion and Quantum Leap Energy development expenditure, compresses that range somewhat; net-cash positions following equity raises tend to be partially offset within quarters by operating burn. A midpoint EV of approximately $350 million to $450 million is the working basis for the multiples analysis that follows.

## Current Multiples and the Revenue-Based Anchor

Against forward revenue estimates derived from disclosed offtake commitments across the Si-28, medical, and HALEU product lines, ASPI trades at elevated EV/Sales multiples consistent with a company whose revenue inflection is anticipated but not yet delivered. If one assigns a conservative $15 to $25 million of recognised revenue for fiscal year 2025 — drawing on initial enriched isotope deliveries, early-stage research contracts, and partial offtake conversion — the trailing EV/Sales multiple spans roughly 15x to 30x depending on the EV anchor used. Forward estimates, which analysts must construct from management's disclosed capacity build-out timelines rather than a conventional guidance framework, compress that multiple toward 8x to 15x on a two-year horizon if ramp assumptions hold.

Price-to-book is calculable, though the denominator is itself volatile given the pace of capital raises. Tangible book value per share, as reported in the most recent balance sheet, reflects the accumulated investment in enrichment centrifuge hardware, Pretoria facility infrastructure, and working capital — partially offset by accumulated operating losses that erode retained earnings. On this basis, the stock trades at a meaningful premium to book, consistent with the market assigning option value to the franchise rather than simply marking the physical assets. No trailing P/E is meaningful. The PEG ratio is inapplicable until sustained earnings materialise.

## The Multiple History: From Speculative Enthusiasm to Recalibration

ASPI listed publicly at a moment when the broader isotope-enrichment narrative commanded a significant valuation premium. Early trading sessions assigned market capitalisations well above $500 million on minimal revenues, reflecting investor excitement about the ASP technology's differentiated cost structure versus incumbent gas-centrifuge enrichment, the IBM-adjacent Si-28 semiconductor thesis, and the HALEU supply-gap story as the NRC's advanced-reactor licensing queue lengthened. That initial premium was followed by a multi-period de-rating as operating losses continued and revenue conversion from offtake announcements proved slower than the most optimistic investor models assumed. Dilution from equity raises — necessary to fund the Pretoria expansion and Quantum Leap Energy's Iceland site development — applied further mechanical downward pressure on per-share valuations even when the enterprise-level story held.

By the 2025-2026 period, the stock had re-rated into a range more consistent with early-stage enrichment infrastructure rather than a fully validated commercial operation. The direction of the next re-rating depends on whether the first material Si-28 semiconductor contracts convert to recognised revenue on schedule, whether the medical isotope supply agreements with radiopharmaceutical customers translate into consistent quarterly line items, and whether Quantum Leap Energy secures credible HALEU offtake commitments from named advanced-reactor developers.

## Peer-Group Comparison

Building a meaningful peer set for ASPI requires mixing established isotope producers, speculative nuclear-technology companies, and early-stage enrichment infrastructure plays. No single peer is a clean analogue.

| Company | Ticker | EV/Sales (fwd 1Y est.) | EV/EBITDA | Stage | Primary overlap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ASP Isotopes | ASPI | ~10–18× | NM (neg.) | Early revenue | All three platforms |
| Centrus Energy | LEU | ~1.5–2.5× | ~10–14× | Revenue-generating | HALEU / enrichment |
| BWX Technologies | BWXT | ~2.5–3.5× | ~14–17× | Mature | Nuclear services / isotopes |
| Eckert & Ziegler | EUZ.DE | ~2.0–3.0× | ~10–13× | Mature | Medical isotopes |
| Oklo | OKLO | NM (pre-rev.) | NM | Pre-revenue | Advanced reactor / HALEU demand |
| Lightbridge Corp. | LTBR | NM (pre-rev.) | NM | Pre-revenue | Speculative nuclear fuel tech |

*Multiples are approximate, drawn from analyst consensus and market data available through the frozen snapshot. Centrus, BWX, and Eckert & Ziegler represent the established-operator baseline; Oklo and Lightbridge represent the speculative-stage comparables.*

The gap between ASPI's implied EV/Sales and those of established isotope operators like Eckert & Ziegler or Centrus is stark. That gap is the market's option premium on the ASP technology's theorised cost advantage and the breadth of the three-platform portfolio. Shrinking it requires sustained revenue delivery — not just further offtake announcements — which is precisely the execution risk the multiple encodes.

## What the Implied DCF Requires

Back-solving from a midpoint enterprise value of roughly $400 million, a simple DCF framework — using an 18 to 22 percent discount rate appropriate for early-stage industrial technology with binary execution risk — implies that the market expects aggregate undiscounted free cash flow of approximately $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion over a ten- to fifteen-year horizon before any terminal value. That figure requires ASPI to ultimately achieve operating margins consistent with a scaled specialty enrichment business — call it 25 to 35 percent EBITDA margins at steady state — on a revenue base somewhere in the $150 million to $300 million range, reached by the early-to-mid 2030s. Every one of those assumptions rests on a chain of dependencies: Pretoria capacity scaling on schedule, semiconductor customers validating Si-28 in production nodes, medical isotope quality qualification cycles completing on target, and Quantum Leap Energy securing both HALEU offtake and project finance before the advanced-reactor fuel gap becomes acute. None of these are guaranteed. All of them are plausible.

## Bull, Base, and Bear Scenarios

**Bull case — $9 to $14 per share.** The bull case assumes that ASPI reaches $80 to $120 million in annual revenue by fiscal year 2028, driven by Si-28 contracts with two or more named semiconductor customers contributing meaningful volume, successful scale-up of Mo-100 and Yb-176 production tied to growing radiopharmaceutical demand, and a Quantum Leap Energy HALEU offtake agreement with at least one named advanced-reactor developer signed before year-end 2027. In this scenario, the market re-rates ASPI toward a 6x to 8x forward EV/Sales multiple on 2028 estimates, with a path to EBITDA breakeven visible within three to four years. The resulting price target — discounted back to 2026 — implies a share price in the upper single digits to low teens. The operative assumption is that dilution from remaining capital raises is modest and that the ASP process proves out at commercial scale without significant engineering setbacks.

**Base case — $3 to $6 per share.** The base case assumes revenue reaches $30 to $50 million annually by fiscal year 2027-2028, with Si-28 contributing a meaningful but not dominant share, medical isotopes building steadily, and Quantum Leap Energy remaining in a development-stage posture with a signed letter of intent but not a binding offtake. The stock trades in a range broadly consistent with its 2025-2026 observed price band: investors assign value to the optionality and technology differentiation, but discount for execution risk and continued dilution. EV/Sales multiples remain elevated — 8x to 12x forward — reflecting unproven but credible scale-up. This is the scenario the current price most closely reflects.

**Bear case — $0.75 to $2 per share.** The bear case is driven by two scenarios that are different in character but convergent in price impact. The first is sustained execution failure: Si-28 semiconductor qualification cycles stall as customers determine that the performance advantage at sub-3nm node does not justify a single-source supply dependency, and medical offtake agreements are renegotiated at lower volumes. The second is dilution-driven: repeated equity raises at successively lower prices to fund widening cash burn compress per-share value even if enterprise value holds nominally steady. In either scenario, the stock drifts back toward cash-adjusted book value or below, and the HALEU optionality in Quantum Leap Energy is valued at near-zero pending demonstrable reactor-fuel contracts.

## The Gap Between Consensus and This Dossier's Read

The market, at present, is pricing in a version of the base case with optionality on the bull. What the dossier's analysis suggests is that consensus modelling tends to underweight two specific risks. First, the timeline mismatch between offtake announcement and revenue recognition is systematically wider than management guidance implies, because semiconductor customer qualification cycles and radiopharmaceutical regulatory approval timelines are both measured in years, not quarters. Second, the Quantum Leap Energy HALEU thesis — which carries meaningful weight in the most optimistic investor decks — is dependent on advanced-reactor project finance timelines that are notoriously difficult to compress, regardless of the underlying technology's merit. A market that assigns full option value to both threads simultaneously may be double-counting probability on correlated timelines.

The dossier's read is that ASPI warrants a base-case valuation consistent with the lower half of the observed 2026 trading range, with a clear path to re-rating only upon conversion of two or more named, material offtake agreements into recognised quarterly revenues. Until that conversion is visible in reported financials — rather than in press releases — the current EV/Sales premium asks investors to extend substantial good faith on a multi-year execution programme across three technically distinct enrichment platforms simultaneously.

chapters.title: Quarterly cadence through customer offtake announcements and capacity scaling
chapters.body:
## 2023: Contracts Before Capacity

ASP Isotopes entered its first full calendar year as a publicly listed company — it had listed on NASDAQ in November 2022 — with a revenue line that barely cleared half a million dollars and operating losses that told a different story entirely. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2023, the company recorded $0.43 million in revenue against an operating loss of $16.0 million and a net loss of $16.3 million, a burn rate that reflected an enrichment program still wholly in the construction and pre-commissioning phase at its Pretoria, South Africa facilities.

What the income statement obscured, however, was a commercial sequence that would later define the company's pitch to investors. In June 2023, ASP Isotopes signed its first multi-year supply agreement for enriched carbon-14 — a take-or-pay contract with a North American customer structured at a minimum annual revenue commitment of $2.5 million, channelled through its commercial partner RC14 Inc. By August, the company announced it had secured a second supply contract with a U.S.-based customer for highly enriched isotopes valued at approximately $9 million in expected aggregate revenue, with a prepayment of roughly $900,000 expected in Q3 2023. Combined, the North American signed pipeline exceeded $11.5 million in anticipated cumulative revenues — a figure that comfortably eclipsed the installed capacity to deliver.

In September 2023, the company signalled its most consequential structural move of the year: the formation of Quantum Leap Energy LLC, a new U.S.-incorporated subsidiary, alongside an operating entity in the United Kingdom, Quantum Leap Energy Ltd. The subsidiary's explicit mission was the development and commercialisation of the company's second proprietary enrichment method — the Quantum Enrichment Process — targeting High Assay Low Enriched Uranium for advanced reactor fuel and lithium-6 for fusion applications. Within weeks of QLE's launch, ASP Isotopes disclosed a first memorandum of understanding with a U.S.-based small modular reactor operator for future HALEU supply. A second MOU with a separate unnamed SMR company followed in November 2023, suggesting a deliberate strategy of parallel engagement rather than exclusive commitment. By December, the company had begun processing raw uranium feed at Pretoria for C-14 production runs, validating the Aerodynamic Separation Process at commercial scale for the first time.

## 2024: The Si-28 Offtake Sequence

On April 1, 2024 — the same day the company announced its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2023 results — ASP Isotopes disclosed a purchase agreement with an unnamed leading U.S. semiconductor manufacturer for the supply of highly enriched silicon-28, the isotope believed to enable next-generation quantum computing qubits and improved AI-chip performance by eliminating nuclear-spin decoherence.

> "To create faster, smaller next-generation semiconductors, the world is likely going to require materials that are currently not available in commercial quantities." — Paul Mann, Chairman and CEO, April 2024

The Pretoria Si-28 facility was at that point still under construction, with an initial nameplate estimate of 10 kilograms per year. A second purchase order followed in June 2024, this time from a leading global industrial gases company that would act as a distribution intermediary into semiconductor supply chains. The two agreements, placed by parties that the company declined to name for competitive reasons, established proof of commercial demand before a single kilogram had shipped.

The quarterly financial cadence through the middle of the year remained modest by conventional standards. Revenue for Q1 2024 came in at approximately $840,000; Q2 added $1.02 million; Q3 contributed $1.09 million. The nine months ended September 30, 2024 aggregated to $2.95 million in revenue against an operating loss for the same period of $18.7 million — losses driven by accelerating construction expenditure, Pretoria operating costs, and the corporate overhead of a dual-segment NASDAQ-listed issuer.

The decisive event of Q4 2024 arrived at the end of October: on October 30, ASP Isotopes announced a non-binding term sheet with TerraPower, LLC, Bill Gates's advanced fission development company, under which TerraPower would provide construction funding for a HALEU enrichment facility to be developed through Quantum Leap Energy and would commit to a ten-year offtake of all production. ASPI shares closed 19.8% higher on the day. Paul Mann's statement framed the deal around technology differentiation rather than volume:

> "Over the last several decades, the scientists at ASP Isotopes have developed some of the world's most advanced isotope enrichment technologies. This term sheet is further validation of our belief that ASP Isotopes can offer scalable and capital efficient technology solutions to the supply challenges which exist in global isotope markets." — Paul Mann, October 30, 2024

One day later the company launched an underwritten equity offering, with Canaccord Genuity acting as sole bookrunner. It closed on November 4 with 2,754,250 shares sold at $6.75 per share — gross proceeds of $18.6 million, with the underwriter's overallotment option exercised in full. Stated use of proceeds: general corporate purposes, including accelerating construction of enrichment facilities in South Africa and Iceland. On November 26, the company announced completion of construction of the Si-28 enrichment facility in Pretoria and commencement of commissioning, with revised pre-commissioning data indicating nameplate capacity had expanded to more than 50 kilograms per year enriched to 99.995% — a fivefold increase over initial design estimates.

| Period | Revenue | Operating Loss | Net Loss | Cash / Equivalents |
|--------|---------|---------------|----------|--------------------|
| FY 2023 | $0.43M | ($16.0M) | ($16.3M) | — |
| FY 2024 | $4.14M | ($26.4M) | ($32.4M) | $61.9M |

For the full year ended December 31, 2024, ASP Isotopes reported revenue of $4.14 million — nearly tenfold the prior year's print — alongside capital expenditures of $9.7 million, up 315% year-over-year, and a long-term debt position of just $1.4 million, reflecting the predominantly equity-financed structure Mann had cultivated since listing.

## 2025: Commercial Production, Definitive Agreements, and a $345 Million Year

Commercial production of enriched silicon-28 commenced at the second ASP enrichment facility in Pretoria in March 2025. In April, Ytterbium-176 — used in the production of lutetium-177 for targeted cancer radiotherapy — entered commercial production at the company's third facility on the same Pretoria campus. The twin commissioning events transformed ASP Isotopes from a construction-stage enrichment developer into a multi-isotope producer, if one still measured in grams and kilograms rather than metric tonnes.

The HALEU chapter reached a new level of formality on May 19, 2025, when ASP Isotopes and TerraPower converted the October term sheet into a suite of definitive agreements. Under the loan agreement, TerraPower committed conditional funding through a multi-advance term loan to a wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary of ASPI for construction of a new uranium enrichment facility at Pelindaba, South Africa — home to the South African Nuclear Energy Corporation, Necsa — with target annual capacity of approximately 15 metric tons of uranium. Initial HALEU production was projected to begin in 2027, subject to licensing. The supply agreement contemplated delivery of HALEU for the initial fuel core of TerraPower's Natrium sodium-cooled fast reactor in Wyoming, with a ten-year framework running from 2028 through 2037 for up to 150 metric tons in total.

> "Nuclear fuel has one of the most severely compromised supply chains of any material in the world." — Paul Mann, May 19, 2025

Capital activity in 2025 ran in parallel. In early June, the company placed a registered direct offering of 7,518,797 shares at $6.65 per share with a single institutional investor for gross proceeds of $50 million, with Cantor and Canaccord Genuity acting as joint bookrunners; proceeds were earmarked partly for a bridge loan facility associated with the acquisition of Renergen Limited, a South African helium and liquefied natural gas producer that broadened ASPI's asset base beyond isotopes. In aggregate, the company raised more than $345 million across equity transactions during FY2025.

First enriched Si-28 samples shipped to a prospective semiconductor customer in August 2025. Ytterbium-176 samples followed in September, at an indicated commercial price of $20,000 per gram, against a targeted production rate of one kilogram per year versus customer demand indications of approximately two kilograms — a supply-demand gap that management described as supportive of pricing discipline.

Full-year 2025 revenue came in at $23.8 million: $5.7 million in product revenue (primarily from PET Labs radiopharmaceuticals acquired during the year) and $18.1 million in construction services revenue generated through the Skyline construction subsidiary. That 480% top-line expansion over 2024's $4.1 million nonetheless sat atop a widening operating loss of $59.9 million and a net loss of $175.1 million — the latter inflated by non-cash charges and non-controlling-interest allocations tied to the company's increasingly complex group structure.

At the Q4 2025 earnings webinar, Paul Mann positioned the trajectory as an inflection rather than an aberration:

> "Our transition to a commercial operations platform marks a pivotal moment for the company. We are no longer a development stage company. We are a critical materials platform." — Paul Mann, Q4 2025 earnings call

The distinction mattered for how investors would read the forward pipeline. Three Si-28 purchase agreements were in place by year-end 2025, with the company targeting low-single-digit million dollars of isotope revenue from silicon in 2026 as qualification cycles completed and commercial shipments began. Ytterbium-176 commercial deliveries were targeted for mid-year 2026. The C-14 take-or-pay contract, at $2.5 to $5 million per year, remained the most structurally protected revenue line — a floor the company had held since 2023. And the HALEU subsidiary, now with a signed loan and supply agreement with one of the most credible names in advanced fission development, sat on a construction runway toward first production that management pegged to 2027. The gap between signed contract and recognised revenue — characteristically 12 to 24 months given enrichment lead times and customer product qualification cycles — had not closed. But heading into 2026, the distance between the two was measurably shorter than it had been when the first contracts were signed with a facility still under construction.

---
